name: The manna hoarders
charge: Keeping manna overnight; going out to gather on the Sabbath
summary: The whole congregation murmured for the flesh pots of Egypt, and the Lord answered with bread from heaven and a test: a daily portion, to prove whether they would walk in his law or not. Some kept it till morning and it bred worms and stank. Told that the sixth day’s double portion was for the sabbath, some went out on the seventh day to gather and found none. The sabbath was already binding in the wilderness.
offenseFull: The whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, wishing they had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt when they sat by the flesh pots and ate bread to the full (Exodus 16:2-3). When deliverance does not come easy, the people turn on the man sent to them. Moses answered that their murmurings were not against him and Aaron but against the Lord: complaining against the leadership the Most High sets up is murmuring against the Most High himself (Exodus 16:8). The Lord said he would rain bread from heaven, and the people would go out and gather a certain rate every day, that he might prove them, whether they would walk in his law or not (Exodus 16:4). They did not know what it was and said one to another, it is manna, which means, what is it; and Moses told them it was the bread the Lord had given them to eat (Exodus 16:15). Every man gathered according to his eating, and he that gathered much had nothing over and he that gathered little had no lack (Exodus 16:17-18): the portion was measured to the appetite and the household, because nourishment is not the same for everybody.

Man does not live by bread only, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of the Lord, and that is what the Lord was proving by a daily portion (Deuteronomy 8:3; Matthew 4:4). The manna is the bread from heaven that speaks of Christ, and our fathers all ate the same spiritual meat and drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ (John 6:31-33; 1 Corinthians 10:1-4). Moses told them that no man was to leave any of it until the morning; some did not listen and left it until the morning, and it bred worms and stank (Exodus 16:19-20). Yesterday’s portion is not enough for today. Job esteemed the words of his mouth more than his necessary food, and Jeremiah found the words and ate them, and they were the joy and rejoicing of his heart (Job 23:12; Jeremiah 15:16). On the sixth day they gathered twice as much, and Moses said the next day was the rest of the holy sabbath to the Lord, so they were to bake and seethe that day what they would and lay up the rest; and what was laid up for the sabbath did not stink nor breed a worm (Exodus 16:22-24). Some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather, and found none (Exodus 16:27).
judgmentFull: The hoarded bread rotted, and Moses was wroth with them (Exodus 16:20). To the sabbath gatherers the Lord asked how long they refused to keep his commandments and his laws, and set the reason beside it: because the Lord had given them the sabbath, he gave them on the sixth day the bread of two days, and every man was to abide in his place and not go out on the seventh day (Exodus 16:28-29). The sabbath was binding before Sinai. Abiding in his place is about not going out to gather food on the sabbath, and it does not undo the holy convocation of the seventh day in all your dwellings, which is a gathering (Leviticus 23:3).

The sentences were small and exact, a stink and an empty basket, given so that the daily portion and the sabbath would be understood before the greater tests came. An omer of the very manna that spoiled overnight was laid up before the Testimony and kept for the generations, that they might see the bread the Lord fed Israel with in the wilderness (Exodus 16:32-34), and Israel ate manna forty years, until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan (Exodus 16:35). The petition for daily bread sits in a prayer that is otherwise wholly about the kingdom, and it is that same lesson set where it cannot be missed (Matthew 6:11). These things are our examples, so that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted; they were not overthrown by an enemy in the wilderness, but by their own appetite (1 Corinthians 10:5-6).

lawsResolved.text: Provide for food needed on the Sabbath in advance so it need not be gathered or bought or cooked on the Sabbath.

Six days of the week are to be used for labor, and the seventh day to be a Sabbath of rest in which you shall do no work. Exod. 16:22-30; Exod. 20:9-11; Exod. 23:12; Exod. 31:15; Exod. 34:21; Exod. 35:2; Lev, 23:3;
You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.
We are not to have a primary desire for earthly things.

text.text: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness:

And the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

And Moses said, This shall be, when the Lord shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that the Lord heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord.

Then said the Lord unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.
And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.
And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.

And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live.
But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
And did all eat the same spiritual meat;
And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.
And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.
Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.
Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.
And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.

And he said unto them, This is that which the Lord hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.
And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.
Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.
And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?
See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.

And Moses said, This is the thing which the Lord commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.
And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the Lord, to be kept for your generations.
As the Lord commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.
Give us this day our daily bread.
But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.

This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, according to the number of your persons; take ye every man for them which are in his tents.
And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.
And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.
And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.
Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.
And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.

And he said unto them, This is that which the Lord hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.
And Moses said, Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath unto the Lord: to day ye shall not find it in the field.
Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.
And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.
And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?
See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
So the people rested on the seventh day.
And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness:

And the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

Then said the Lord unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

And Moses said, This is the thing which the Lord commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.
And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the Lord, to be kept for your generations.
As the Lord commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.
